record.context_brief: additional harmonic maps from the disc to the sphere
record.original_question: Let Omega be the unit disc in R^2 and consider harmonic maps u: Omega -> S^2 satisfying Delta u_i = u_i |grad u|^2 for i=1,2,3, |u|=1 in Omega, and u=g on the boundary. For the boundary condition g(x,y)=(R x, R y, sqrt(1-R^2)) with 0<R<1, the source gives two explicit solutions u and u_bar, with parameters lambda = 1/R + sqrt(1/R^2 - 1) and mu = 1/R - sqrt(1/R^2 - 1). Are there any solutions of this harmonic-map boundary value problem other than those two explicit solutions?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3.1 ([22]). Assume that g is given by (3.4). Are there other solutions of (3.1)-(3.3) besides u and u_bar?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be the open unit disc. Consider maps $u = (u_1, u_2, u_3): \Omega \to S^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ that are weakly harmonic in the sense that they satisfy the Euler–Lagrange system for the Dirichlet energy:
$$\Delta u_i = u_i\, |\nabla u|^2, \qquad i = 1, 2, 3, \qquad |u| = 1 \text{ in } \Omega,$$
with prescribed boundary data
$$u(x,y) = g(x,y) \text{ on } \partial\Omega.$$
Fix a constant $R \in (0,1)$ and choose the boundary datum
$$g(x,y) = \bigl(Rx,\, Ry,\, \sqrt{1-R^2}\bigr), \qquad (x,y) \in \partial\Omega,$$
which maps $\partial\Omega$ onto a horizontal circle of latitude on $S^2$. Define
$$\lambda = \frac{1}{R} + \sqrt{\frac{1}{R^2} - 1}, \qquad \mu = \frac{1}{R} - \sqrt{\frac{1}{R^2} - 1},$$
and consider the two explicit solutions of the above boundary value problem given (in terms of $z = x+iy$) by
$$u(z) = \left(\frac{2\,\mathrm{Re}\,(\lambda z)}{|\lambda z|^2+1},\, \frac{2\,\mathrm{Im}\,(\lambda z)}{|\lambda z|^2+1},\, \frac{|\lambda z|^2 - 1}{|\lambda z|^2+1}\right),$$
$$\bar u(z) = \left(\frac{2\,\mathrm{Re}\,(\mu z)}{|\mu z|^2+1},\, \frac{2\,\mathrm{Im}\,(\mu z)}{|\mu z|^2+1},\, \frac{|\mu z|^2 - 1}{|\mu z|^2+1}\right),$$
both of which match the boundary datum $g$ on $\partial\Omega$.

Question: Does the above boundary value problem admit any weakly harmonic map solution $\Omega \to S^2$ other than $u$ and $\bar u$?

artifact.status_search_result: Web searches reveal extensive literature on the Dirichlet problem for harmonic maps from the disc into $S^2$ (Brezis–Coron, Jost, Soyeur, and later work on symmetric boundary data and symmetry-breaking), establishing existence of multiple solutions and symmetry phenomena, but no source was found that explicitly resolves the uniqueness-up-to-the-two-explicit-solutions question for this specific axially symmetric latitude-circle boundary datum. The status is therefore not clearly determined by the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Symmetric boundary values for the Dirichlet problem for harmonic maps from the disc into the 2-sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Studies multiple solutions of the Dirichlet problem for harmonic maps with symmetric boundary data, exhibiting multiple solutions in many homotopy classes.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on multiplicity of solutions for this Dirichlet problem with symmetric boundary values, with no definitive uniqueness result identified for the specific latitude-circle boundary datum.

status_evidence.title: Multiple solutions of the Dirichlet problem for harmonic maps from discs into 2-spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of at least two solutions in distinct homotopy classes for non-constant boundary data.
status_evidence.claim: Brezis–Coron / Jost prove existence of at least two distinct solutions, but do not classify all solutions for the specific axisymmetric boundary datum in question.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry breaking for the Dirichlet problem for harmonic maps from the disc into the 2-sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Studies symmetry-breaking phenomena which can produce additional solutions beyond symmetric ones.
status_evidence.claim: Symmetry-breaking results suggest the possibility of further solutions, but no decisive resolution of the stated problem was located.
